answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The marble multiplier is published, charged in quill, and comet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2469 identities would post 1486 proofs and burn roughly 26 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
